notes: Fixes both reported problems: a reusable caller with children now takes its status from those children through RefreshReusableCallerStatus, so it stays cancelling until the runner acknowledges, and cancelRun now emits the run when no jobs changed, so blocked concurrency waiters wake up; the main risks are that the caller fix depends on children being cancelled before their caller, the no-children branch duplicates the existing task-less cancel code, and nesting below one level is not tested.

The fix addresses both root causes: a reusable caller with children now takes its status from them through RefreshReusableCallerStatus, so it stays cancelling until the runner acknowledges, and a cancel that changes no jobs now emits the run so blocked concurrency waiters wake up. The tests are realistic and cover the acknowledgement cascade and force-cancel waking a waiter. Minor nits: the no-children branch duplicates the direct-cancel code, the caller is returned as 'updated' even when its status did not change, and nested callers are not tested.

The patch fixes the root cause in the header parser and also centralises a `ParseableDiffPrefixes` builder that forces `noprefix=false`, `srcPrefix=a/` and `dstPrefix=b/` on every diff lazygit parses, including the worktree and stash diffs that previously had no override. It leaves mnemonicPrefix alone, which is sound because git ignores the custom prefixes when mnemonic mode is on and its prefixes are strippable single components. It adds `rename to`/`copy to` fallback parsing as the spec asks; most of the parser rewrite and any new parser tests are truncated, but hidden tests pass, and the visible test changes only update the expected command arguments.

Fixes the root cause on both sides: the header parser now strips any single-component prefix, falls back to `rename to`/`copy to` lines, and splits unquoting from prefix stripping, while a new `ParseableDiffPrefixes` builder step forces stripable prefixes on lazygit's own diffs (including the worktree diff and stash show, which previously lacked it) and deliberately leaves mnemonicPrefix alone. All hidden tests pass. The diff is truncated, so the stripping and `diff --git` splitting logic and any new parser tests cannot be checked; the visible test changes only update argv expectations, and touching the name-status loader is harmless but unnecessary.

Adds `--links` translation to both zip and squashfs, with the required skip notice, an escape guard and broad tests, but one hidden test fails. It has gaps: a regular `x.rclonelink` beside a symlink `x` gives duplicate list entries, so listing and `NewObject` disagree. A zip root pointing at `link.rclonelink` is not resolved. The `dt[""] = nil` root workaround and the special-cased EOF in `Open` are slightly hacky.

Covers the main spec for both zip and squashfs: links are skipped without --links with a flag-naming notice, listed with the .rclonelink suffix and readable with seek/range, and hostile members inside a symlink are dropped. However, a regular `foo.rclonelink` plus a symlink `foo` produce duplicate listings, single-object roots behave differently between zip and squashfs, and one hidden test fails.

Walks the type-checked CEL AST to collect the literal names passed to `ph()` calls and records an empty name when the name is dynamic. It then treats a matcher set as a response condition only if one of those names is status_code, status_text, a latency placeholder, a `header.*` placeholder, or unknown. This covers every case the maintainers listed: shorthand, direct `ph` calls, escaped literals, upstream.host and status_codes. The tests are thorough and actually exercise expressions that evaluate true. The new public `Placeholders()` API on MatchExpression is a slightly broader surface than strictly needed.

The patch finds the root cause. It walks the type-checked CEL AST for `ph(req, ...)` calls, which covers both the `{placeholder}` shorthand and direct `ph` calls. Only exact response placeholders (status_code, status_text, the two latency ones) and the `header.` prefix trigger response retries, while non-literal names stay conservatively retryable. This correctly covers escaped literals, near-miss names such as `status_codes`, and upstream-selection placeholders. The tests are strong, with unit tests for `Placeholders()` and table-driven proxy tests that would fail without the fix. Minor nits: a new exported API method, and the placeholder slice is cloned and rescanned on every response instead of being precomputed at provision time.

Fixes the root cause by removing the leaked dup'd `File()` fds in both `Close` and the reuse path, and unlinks via `Addr()` under the mutex. It meets every review requirement: refcounted unlink, a CAS guard that returns `net.ErrClosed` on double close, safe close/relisten races, and an abstract-socket guard that also stops unlinking on listen. One weakness carries over from before: the map can still point at a closed newest wrapper if that holder closes first. Tests are thorough, though the abstract test writes a sentinel file into the package directory.

Fixes the root cause: Close() no longer dups the fd via File(), which had kept the socket listening until GC, and it now unlinks the real path from Addr() instead of the bogus File().Name(). It also closes the leaked dup in reuseUnixSocket, adds an atomic closed flag so a second Close returns ErrClosed, holds unixSocketsMu across decrement/close/unlink so a racing relisten is safe, and skips unlink for Linux abstract sockets on both listen and close. Thorough tests cover each requirement; minor nits are that the new package-level isAbstractUnixSocket is shadowed by a same-named local in listen.go, and a map entry left pointing at an already-closed holder is not repaired (a pre-existing issue).

The patch follows the maintainer's design and the hidden PR tests pass. It adds `Close` to the interface, makes `Get`/`Walk` reconnect a closed connection, and resets the engine ID, boots, time, localized keys and `ContextEngineID` when reconnecting a closed connection. The plugin closes the connection on any field or table error. Weak points: the package suite fails; the reset also wipes user-configured engine_id/boots/time, even when the initial connect simply failed; the close happens only after all tables, so later tables in the same gather still use the stale session; and it makes unrelated environment-workaround edits to `TestSnmpInitGosmi`.

The core fix looks sound: it adds `Close()` to the interface, `Close` and `Reconnect`-on-nil-Conn reset the USM engine ID, boots, time, keys and context engine ID, `Get`/`Walk` reconnect first, and `Gather` closes the agent's connection after any top-level or table error, with `StopOnError` preserved; but the package suite fails, the reset also wipes programmatically configured engine params on a first lazy connect, and it carries an unrelated environment-specific rewrite of `TestSnmpInitGosmi` (path and logger).

Tracking each series' latest exemplar timestamp and keeping exemplar-bearing series alive in gc/gcSeries is a plausible design, but it fails all 3 hidden tests and the package suite. The truncated diff does not show that the protection is restored on WAL or snapshot replay, so the restart cases are likely wrong; the many new tests do not save a patch that breaks the suite.

Tracking each series' max exemplar timestamp and keeping exemplar-protected series through gc/gcSeries is a plausible design, but it fails all hidden tests and the package suite, likely because the changed stripeSeries.gc/gcSeries signatures break existing callers or the replay/snapshot paths are incomplete. The extensive new tests therefore cannot be trusted to validate the fix.
